methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $1.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
JetZero is a Series B-stage transportation company founded by Tom O'Leary and Mark Page that has raised $1.0B+ to date. The transportation sector comprises 8 private peers (including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, and Parallel Systems) and no direct public comparables. The private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints to support median-based peer valuation, limiting triangulation to stage-progression methodology.

Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $1.0B total-raised proxy, yielding a $1.9B implied valuation. This single-method result anchors the analysis given the narrow peer universe and sparse transportation-sector comparables at JetZero's tier.

The triangulated range spans $1.6B (low) to $2.2B (high), centered on $1.9B median. This range reflects the inherent uncertainty of relying on one applicable methodology and the absence of narrow peer-valuation anchors. Key sensitivities include the appropriateness of the 1.9x multiplier to frontier-transportation dynamics and the assumption that total capital raised reasonably proxies for recent fair value. Materiality derives from comparable companies' stage transitions and sector-specific capital intensity, neither of which the current dataset quantifies with precision.
